questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Cornea:
options: Has an endothelial layer that regenerates readily.
Has an epithelial layer that fails to regenerate.
The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma.
Is an important refractive component of the eye.
Has a stroma composed of randomly arranged collagen fibrils.
originalOptions: Has an endothelial layer that regenerates readily.
Has an epithelial layer that fails to regenerate.
The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma.
Is an important refractive component of the eye.
Has a stroma composed of randomly arranged collagen fibrils.
questions.correctAnswer: C) The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma. / D) Is an important refractive component of the eye.
questions.correctAnswerText: C) The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma. / D) Is an important refractive component of the eye.
questions.explanation: A) False. The human endothelium does not regenerate; dead cells are replaced by the spreading of surviving cells. B) False. The epithelial layer readily regenerates. C) True. The endothelial cells pump out ions and the water follows osmotically. Removal of water maintains corneal transparency. D) True. The cornea is a more powerful refractive element than the natural lens of the eye. E) False. The fine, equally spaced, stromal collagen fibrils are arranged in parallel and packed in an orderly manner. This is a requirement for transparency.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Retina:
options: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve.
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision.
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the retinal pigment epithelium.
The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
originalOptions: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve.
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision.
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the retinal pigment epithelium.
The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Is ten layers thick. / B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve. / E) The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
questions.correctAnswerText: A) Is ten layers thick. / B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve. / E) The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
questions.explanation: A) True. B) True. The retinal ganglion cell axons form the retinal nerve fibre layer and exit the eye at the optic nerve head. C) False. The rods are responsible for night vision and three cone types are responsible for daylight and colour vision. D) False. The attachment is loose; the neuroretina separates from the RPE in retinal detachment. E) True. Vitamin A is delivered by the RPE to the photoreceptors and combined with opsin.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Lens:
options: Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule.
Cortex and nucleus are rich in organelles.
Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content.
Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
originalOptions: Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule.
Cortex and nucleus are rich in organelles.
Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content.
Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Grows throughout life. / B) Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule. / D) Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content. / E) Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
questions.correctAnswerText: A) Grows throughout life. / B) Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule. / D) Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content. / E) Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
questions.explanation: A) True. It does grow throughout life. B) True. This is of great importance in cataract surgery. C) False. The older, deep cortical and nuclear fibres lose their nuclei and other organelles. D) True. The high protein content accounts for its high refractive index. E) True.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Suspensory ligament of the lens (the zonule):
options: Attaches the lens to the ciliary body.
Is part of the iridocorneal angle.
Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
originalOptions: Attaches the lens to the ciliary body.
Is part of the iridocorneal angle.
Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Attaches the lens to the ciliary body. / D) Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
questions.correctAnswerText: A) Attaches the lens to the ciliary body. / D) Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
questions.explanation: A) True. Zonular fibres extend from the pars plicata of the ciliary body to the lens equator. B) False. The zonule lies behind the iris and iridocorneal angle. C) False. The ciliary muscle contains smooth muscle, not the zonule, which is acellular. D) True. Contraction of the ciliary muscle relaxes the zonular fibres allowing the lens to increase its curvature and thus its refractive power (this is ‘accommodation’).

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Posterior chamber:
options: Is another name for the vitreous body.
Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body.
Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes.
Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
originalOptions: Is another name for the vitreous body.
Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body.
Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes.
Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
questions.correctAnswer: B) Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body. / C) Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes. / D) Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
questions.correctAnswerText: B) Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body. / C) Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes. / D) Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
questions.explanation: A) False. The vitreous body is quite separate. B) True. D) True. D) True. Communication is via the pupil, in the gap between iris and lens at the pupil margin. If this gap is narrowed or closed, pressure in the posterior chamber pushes the iris forward and may close the angle (acute closed-angle glaucoma).

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Tear film:
options: Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system.
The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea.
Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye.
originalOptions: Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system.
The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea.
Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye.
questions.correctAnswer: B) Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system. / C) The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea. / D) Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye. / E) Contains lysozyme and secretory IgA.
questions.correctAnswerText: B) Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system. / C) The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea. / D) Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye. / E) Contains lysozyme and secretory IgA.
questions.explanation: A) False. The tear film is about 3 μm thick. B) True. There is a punctum on the medial aspect of both upper and lower eyelids. These allow tears to drain into the nasolacrimal drainage system. C) True. The mucin layer is produced by goblet cells. D) True. It provides a smooth interface for the refraction of light. E) True. These account for the antibacterial properties of the tear film.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Iridocorneal Angle:
options: Is the site of aqueous production.
Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body.
In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork.
Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
originalOptions: Is the site of aqueous production.
Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body.
In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork.
Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
questions.correctAnswer: B) Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body. / C) In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork. / D) Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
questions.correctAnswerText: B) Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body. / C) In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork. / D) Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
questions.explanation: A) False. It is the site of aqueous drainage. B) True. C) True. This may reduce aqueous drainage. D) True. Flow depends on the pressure gradient between the anterior chamber and Schlemm’s canal and there is also an active component.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Optic Nerve:
options: Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate.
Is not bathed in CSF until it enters the cranial cavity.
Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries.
Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve.
Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
originalOptions: Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate.
Is not bathed in CSF until it enters the cranial cavity.
Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries.
Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve.
Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
questions.correctAnswer: A) Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate. / C) Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries. / D) Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve. / E) Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
questions.correctAnswerText: A) Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate. / C) Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries. / D) Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve. / E) Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
questions.explanation: A) True. This sieve-like structure provides support for the optic nerve as it leaves the eye. B) False. In the orbit, outside its pial sheath, the optic nerve is surrounded by cerebrospinal fluid within the subarachnoid space. This is in continuity with that in the intracranial cavity. C) True. The supply to the anterior part of the optic nerve differs from the supply to the anteriorlayers of the retina. D) True. This is a most important blood supply for the anterior optic nerve. E) False. They are usually not myelinated within the eye. F) True. It is made up from retinal ganglion cell axons.

questions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Third, Fourth and Sixth Cranial Nerves:
options: A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus.
The fourth nerve supplies the lateral rectus.
The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course.
The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
originalOptions: A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus.
The fourth nerve supplies the lateral rectus.
The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course.
The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
questions.correctAnswer: B) A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus. / D) The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course. / E) The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
questions.correctAnswerText: B) A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus. / D) The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course. / E) The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
questions.explanation: A) False. The nuclei of the sixth and seventh nerves lie in the pons. B) True. The superior rectus is innervated by the contralateral nucleus. C) False. It supplies the superior oblique. D) True. This makes the sixth nerve susceptible to trauma, which may cause lateral rectus palsy. E) True. It passes lateral to the artery.

questions.text: The tear film:
options: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
Is not important in the refraction of light entering the eye
originalOptions: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
Is not important in the refraction of light entering the eye
questions.correctAnswer: C) The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
questions.correctAnswerText: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
questions.explanation: The tear film is trilaminar (lipid, aqueous, mucin), with the inner mucin layer directly wetting the hydrophobic corneal epithelium — making C correct and B wrong (three layers, not four). A is wrong because the tear film average thickness is only 3 µm (ranging from 2 to 5.5 µm), not 100 µm. D is wrong because the tear-air interface is actually a major refractive surface of the eye, so the tear film is optically important, not irrelevant.

questions.text: Aqueous humour is formed by:
questions.correctAnswer: A) Epithelium of ciliary body
questions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium of ciliary body
questions.explanation: B and C are wrong because the iris and lens play no role in aqueous production — the iris only regulates pupil size, and the lens is purely refractive. D is a plausible-sounding distractor since the pars plana is part of the ciliary body region, but production occurs at the ciliary processes (pars plicata), not the pars plana. E is wrong because the trabecular meshwork is a drainage structure, not a secretory one.

questions.text: All of the following statements about the tear film are true EXCEPT:
options: Lysozyme and lactoferrin in the aqueous layer provide antibacterial protection
The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
The tear film keeps the corneal surface smooth, clear, and lubricated
Conjunctival goblet cells produce the inner mucin layer
The mucin layer allows the aqueous layer to wet the hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly
originalOptions: Lysozyme and lactoferrin in the aqueous layer provide antibacterial protection
The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
The tear film keeps the corneal surface smooth, clear, and lubricated
Conjunctival goblet cells produce the inner mucin layer
The mucin layer allows the aqueous layer to wet the hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly
questions.correctAnswer: B) The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
questions.correctAnswerText: The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
questions.explanation: The meibomian glands, located in the tarsal plates, secrete the outer lipid layer of the tear film, not the aqueous layer — the aqueous layer (about 90% of tear thickness) comes from the main and accessory lacrimal glands, and also carries antibacterial proteins like lysozyme and lactoferrin. A, C, D, and E are all correct descriptions of tear film anatomy.

questions.text: Choose the correct answer about the retina:
options: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the RPE
The RPE delivers vitamin K for rhodopsin production
originalOptions: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the RPE
The RPE delivers vitamin K for rhodopsin production
questions.correctAnswer: B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
questions.correctAnswerText: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
questions.explanation: The retinal ganglion cell axons converge at the optic disc and exit the eye as the optic nerve — this is why the optic disc, lacking photoreceptors, corresponds to the physiological blind spot. A is wrong because the retina has 10 histological layers, not 7. C is wrong on two counts: colour vision is mediated by cones (not rods), and there are three types of cones (not rods). D is wrong because the neurosensory retina is only loosely apposed to the RPE (not firmly attached) — this is exactly why retinal detachment can occur. E is wrong because the RPE recycles vitamin A (not vitamin K) for the visual cycle and rhodopsin regeneration.

questions.text: Most of the thickness of the cornea is formed by:
questions.correctAnswer: B) Substantia propria (stroma)
questions.correctAnswerText: Substantia propria (stroma)
questions.explanation: The stroma (substantia propria) makes up about 90% of corneal thickness. It consists of organized collagen fibers that give the cornea its transparency and structural strength.

questions.text: Cornea is supplied by nerve fibers derived from:
questions.correctAnswer: C) Trigeminal nerve
questions.correctAnswerText: Trigeminal nerve
questions.explanation: The cornea is one of the most densely innervated tissues in the body, supplied sensorially by the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve — which is why corneal inflammation or ulceration is extremely painful.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a source of nutrients to the cornea?
questions.correctAnswer: D) Vitreous humour
questions.correctAnswerText: Vitreous humour
questions.explanation: The cornea is avascular and is nourished by atmospheric oxygen, the aqueous humour, and the perilimbal capillary network. The vitreous humour is not a source of corneal nutrition.

questions.text: All of the following are avascular EXCEPT:
options: None of the above — all are avascular
originalOptions: None of the above — all are avascular
questions.correctAnswer: B) Sclera
questions.correctAnswerText: Sclera
questions.explanation: The cornea and lens are explicitly avascular, nourished only by diffusion, and the vitreous is a clear gel with no vessels of its own. The sclera, in contrast, is a vascularised collagenous coat — it receives blood supply (e.g. via episcleral vessels) unlike the other three purely avascular, diffusion-dependent ocular structures.

questions.text: All of the following are part of the uvea except:
questions.correctAnswer: D) Schwalbe's line
questions.correctAnswerText: Schwalbe's line
questions.explanation: The uvea consists of the iris, ciliary body (which has two parts: pars plicata and pars plana), and the choroid. Schwalbe's line is an anatomical landmark at the anterior chamber angle (the termination of Descemet's membrane) and is not part of the uveal tract.

questions.text: The following is a part of uvea except:
questions.correctAnswer: A) Bowman's membrane
questions.correctAnswerText: Bowman's membrane
questions.explanation: Bowman's membrane is a layer of the cornea and has no relation to the uveal tract.

questions.text: Optic disc diameter is:
questions.correctAnswer: B) 1.5 mm
questions.correctAnswerText: 1.5 mm
questions.explanation: The optic disc diameter is used as a standard unit of measurement (Disc Diameter, DD) to describe the size and location of fundus lesions.

questions.text: Aqueous humour is formed by:
questions.correctAnswer: A) Epithelium of ciliary body
questions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium of ciliary body
questions.explanation: Aqueous humour is secreted by the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium via both active secretion and ultrafiltration.

questions.text: Aqueous humor is secreted by:
questions.correctAnswer: C) Ciliary processes
questions.correctAnswerText: Ciliary processes
questions.explanation: The ciliary processes are the precise anatomical site of aqueous humour secretion within the ciliary body.

questions.text: Corneal ulceration/anaesthesia is caused by injury to the ___ cranial nerve:
questions.correctAnswer: D) Fifth
questions.correctAnswerText: Fifth
questions.explanation: Loss of corneal sensation (from trigeminal nerve injury) abolishes the protective blink reflex, leaving the cornea vulnerable to neurotrophic keratitis.

questions.text: Number of layers in the neurosensory retina is:
questions.explanation: The neurosensory retina classically consists of 9 layers, from the photoreceptors to the nerve fiber layer. The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is anatomically and functionally a separate, tenth layer.

questions.text: The cornea receives its nutrition and oxygen mainly through diffusion. Which of the following is the correct source for its oxygen supply?
questions.correctAnswer: C) Tear film
questions.correctAnswerText: Tear film
questions.explanation: The cornea is avascular and depends entirely on diffusion for nourishment — oxygen comes from the tear film, glucose from the aqueous humour, and the limbal vessels contribute nutrients at the periphery only. This avascularity is essential for maintaining corneal transparency.

questions.text: Arrange the five histological layers of the cornea in correct anterior-to-posterior order:
options: Epithelium → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Endothelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Epithelium
Epithelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Endothelium
Bowman's layer → Epithelium → Stroma → Endothelium → Descemet's membrane
originalOptions: Epithelium → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Endothelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Epithelium
Epithelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Endothelium
Bowman's layer → Epithelium → Stroma → Endothelium → Descemet's membrane
questions.correctAnswer: B) Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
questions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
questions.explanation: The correct anterior-to-posterior sequence is epithelium (regenerates fast) → Bowman's layer (does not regenerate) → stroma (~90% of thickness) → Descemet's membrane (basement membrane) → endothelium (pump layer, does not regenerate).

questions.text: A 32-year-old contact lens wearer with poor hygiene presents with a painful red eye. A corneal scrape grows an organism that rapidly progressed to perforation within 48 hours. Which corneal layer, if breached, is classically unable to regenerate and predisposes to permanent scarring?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Bowman's layer
questions.correctAnswerText: Bowman's layer
questions.explanation: Bowman's layer is tough but does not regenerate if damaged, unlike the epithelium which regenerates within days. This is why deep corneal injuries involving Bowman's layer or beyond tend to leave permanent scarring rather than healing cleanly.

questions.text: The main route of aqueous humour outflow, accounting for approximately 90–96% of drainage, is:
options: The uveoscleral pathway through the ciliary body face
The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
originalOptions: The uveoscleral pathway through the ciliary body face
The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
questions.correctAnswer: C) The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
questions.correctAnswerText: The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
questions.explanation: Aqueous drains conventionally through the trabecular meshwork into Schlemm's canal and then into episcleral veins, accounting for the large majority of outflow; the uveoscleral route handles only about 4–10%. This conventional pathway is the main pharmacological target in glaucoma treatment.

questions.text: All of the following statements about the sclera are true EXCEPT:
options: It is continuous with the cornea at the limbus
It is continuous with the dural sheath of the optic nerve posteriorly
The four rectus muscles insert into it anterior to the equator
It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
It gives the globe its shape and protects intraocular contents
originalOptions: It is continuous with the cornea at the limbus
It is continuous with the dural sheath of the optic nerve posteriorly
The four rectus muscles insert into it anterior to the equator
It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
It gives the globe its shape and protects intraocular contents
questions.correctAnswer: D) It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
questions.correctAnswerText: It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
questions.explanation: The sclera is part of the outer fibrous coat (with the cornea), not the middle vascular coat — the middle vascular coat is the uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, choroid).

questions.text: Which structure is responsible for producing the outer lipid layer of the tear film, and what is its main function?
options: Lacrimal gland; provides 90% of tear thickness
Goblet cells; wets the hydrophobic corneal epithelium
Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
Accessory lacrimal glands; delivers antibacterial proteins
originalOptions: Lacrimal gland; provides 90% of tear thickness
Goblet cells; wets the hydrophobic corneal epithelium
Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
Accessory lacrimal glands; delivers antibacterial proteins
questions.correctAnswer: C) Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
questions.correctAnswerText: Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
questions.explanation: The meibomian glands, located within the tarsal plates, secrete the outer lipid layer whose main job is to slow evaporation of the underlying aqueous layer. Dysfunction of these glands is a major cause of evaporative dry eye.

questions.text: The ciliary body has two principal functions. Select the correct pair:
options: Aqueous humour drainage and pupil constriction
Refraction and pigmentation of the iris
originalOptions: Aqueous humour drainage and pupil constriction
Refraction and pigmentation of the iris
questions.correctAnswer: B) Aqueous humour production and accommodation
questions.correctAnswerText: Aqueous humour production and accommodation
questions.explanation: The ciliary epithelium (non-pigmented layer) produces aqueous humour, while the ciliary muscle mediates accommodation by relaxing the zonular fibres to allow the lens to become more spherical. Loss of this accommodative function with age is the basis of presbyopia.

questions.text: Contraction of which iris muscle produces mydriasis (pupil dilation), and via which autonomic pathway?
questions.correctAnswer: B) Dilator pupillae; sympathetic
questions.correctAnswerText: Dilator pupillae; sympathetic
questions.explanation: The dilator pupillae consists of radial fibres under sympathetic control, producing mydriasis, whereas the sphincter pupillae is circular and parasympathetically innervated (CN III), producing miosis.

questions.text: Which statement about the lens is correct?
options: It is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
It is vascularised to support its constant growth
It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
It stops growing once the eye reaches adult size
It is fixed in position and cannot vary its power
originalOptions: It is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
It is vascularised to support its constant growth
It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
It stops growing once the eye reaches adult size
It is fixed in position and cannot vary its power
questions.correctAnswer: C) It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
questions.correctAnswerText: It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
questions.explanation: The lens contributes about one-third of the eye's ~60 D total refractive power, with the cornea providing the other two-thirds. Unlike the cornea, the lens is the only structure able to vary its power, and it is avascular, continuing to grow throughout life by laying down new fibres.

questions.text: A patient has a dense mature cataract. Which of the following visual functions is expected to be relatively preserved, helping distinguish this from glaucoma?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Peripheral visual field
questions.correctAnswerText: Peripheral visual field
questions.explanation: In lens or macular pathology such as cataract, central acuity is affected while the peripheral field is generally preserved — the opposite pattern to glaucoma, where the peripheral field is lost first and central acuity is preserved until late disease.

questions.text: Cones, responsible for colour vision and fine visual acuity, are exclusively found at which retinal location?
questions.correctAnswer: C) Fovea centralis
questions.correctAnswerText: Fovea centralis
questions.explanation: Cones are concentrated at the macula and are exclusively present at its centre, the fovea centralis, which is the point of sharpest vision. Rods, by contrast, are far more numerous but absent from the very centre of the fovea, mediating dim-light and peripheral vision instead.

questions.text: The optic disc corresponds to the physiological blind spot because:
options: It is the thinnest part of the retina
It is where the vitreous attaches most firmly
originalOptions: It is the thinnest part of the retina
It is where the vitreous attaches most firmly
questions.correctAnswer: B) It contains no photoreceptors
questions.correctAnswerText: It contains no photoreceptors
questions.explanation: The optic disc is where retinal ganglion cell axons converge and exit the eye as the optic nerve; since it contains no photoreceptors, it corresponds to the physiological blind spot. This is distinct from the fovea, which has the highest photoreceptor density.

questions.text: The vitreous body is firmly attached at all of the following sites EXCEPT:
options: The vitreous base, just behind the ora serrata
None of the above — all are correct attachment sites
originalOptions: The vitreous base, just behind the ora serrata
None of the above — all are correct attachment sites
questions.correctAnswer: D) The lens equator
questions.correctAnswerText: The lens equator
questions.explanation: The vitreous is firmly attached at the vitreous base, the optic disc margin, and the macula — these are the sites that matter when the vitreous shrinks and pulls with age, leading to posterior vitreous detachment. It is not described as firmly attached at the lens equator.

questions.text: A 68-year-old man develops sudden painless monocular vision loss. An embolus is suspected to have lodged in a branch of the ophthalmic artery. If the embolus blocks the central retinal artery rather than a posterior ciliary artery, which structure is primarily affected?
options: The optic nerve head via ischaemic optic neuropathy
originalOptions: The optic nerve head via ischaemic optic neuropathy
questions.correctAnswer: C) The retina
questions.correctAnswerText: The retina
questions.explanation: The central retinal artery supplies the retina, so its occlusion causes central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), while blockage of a posterior ciliary artery instead causes ischaemic optic neuropathy by affecting the optic nerve head and choroid. Both vessels arise from the ophthalmic artery, itself one of the first branches of the internal carotid artery.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the anterior chamber and drainage angle?
options: The space between the lens and vitreous, containing vitreous gel
The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
The space posterior to the iris, filled with vitreous
A space found only in angle-closure glaucoma
The space between the retina and choroid
originalOptions: The space between the lens and vitreous, containing vitreous gel
The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
The space posterior to the iris, filled with vitreous
A space found only in angle-closure glaucoma
The space between the retina and choroid
questions.correctAnswer: B) The space between the cornea and iris/lens, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
questions.correctAnswerText: The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
questions.explanation: The anterior chamber lies between the cornea anteriorly and the iris posteriorly, filled with aqueous humour, and the drainage angle at its periphery contains the trabecular meshwork.

questions.text: The conjunctiva contains goblet cells whose function is to:
options: Produce the outer lipid layer of the tear film
Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
Provide sensory innervation to the ocular surface
originalOptions: Produce the outer lipid layer of the tear film
Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
Provide sensory innervation to the ocular surface
questions.correctAnswer: B) Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
questions.correctAnswerText: Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
questions.explanation: Goblet cells within the conjunctiva secrete mucin, which allows the aqueous tear layer to wet the otherwise hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly. The conjunctiva itself has bulbar and palpebral parts meeting at the fornices.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct pairing of a uveal tract structure with its principal role?
options: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
originalOptions: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
questions.correctAnswer: B) Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
questions.correctAnswerText: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
questions.explanation: The choroid is the posterior, vascular part of the uveal tract, and its capillary layer (the choriocapillaris) supplies the outer retina, including the photoreceptors. New vessel growth from the choroid through Bruch's membrane is also the underlying mechanism of wet age-related macular degeneration.

questions.text: A patient has an intraocular pressure of 24 mmHg on tonometry. Which of the following is the accepted normal range for IOP, against which this value should be judged?
questions.correctAnswer: B) 10–21 mmHg
questions.correctAnswerText: 10–21 mmHg
questions.explanation: The normal intraocular pressure range is 10–21 mmHg, set by the balance between aqueous production by the ciliary body and its drainage through the trabecular and uveoscleral routes. A reading of 24 mmHg is therefore above the normal range and warrants further glaucoma work-up.

questions.text: Select all correct statements regarding the three concentric layers of the globe:
options: The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera
The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid
The inner neural coat is the retina
The lens forms part of the outer fibrous coat
The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
originalOptions: The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera
The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid
The inner neural coat is the retina
The lens forms part of the outer fibrous coat
The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
questions.correctAnswer: A) The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera / B) The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid / C) The inner neural coat is the retina / E) The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
questions.correctAnswerText: A) The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera / B) The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid / C) The inner neural coat is the retina / E) The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and E are all true — the globe wall consists of an outer fibrous coat (cornea + sclera), a middle vascular coat (uveal tract: iris + ciliary body + choroid), and an inner neural coat (retina). D is false because the lens is one of the three transparent refracting media inside the globe (with aqueous humour and vitreous), not part of the wall itself.

questions.text: Regarding the refractive power of the eye, which statement is correct?
options: The lens contributes roughly two-thirds and the cornea one-third of total refractive power
The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
The vitreous is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
The sclera contributes significantly to refraction
Refractive power is equally divided among the cornea, lens, and vitreous
originalOptions: The lens contributes roughly two-thirds and the cornea one-third of total refractive power
The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
The vitreous is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
The sclera contributes significantly to refraction
Refractive power is equally divided among the cornea, lens, and vitreous
questions.correctAnswer: B) The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
questions.correctAnswerText: The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
questions.explanation: The cornea provides about two-thirds of the eye's total refractive power (~43 D of the ~60 D total), while the lens contributes the remaining third — though only the lens can vary its own power for accommodation. This distribution is a frequently tested high-yield fact in ophthalmic optics.

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Cornea:
options: Has an endothelial layer that regenerates readily.
Has an epithelial layer that fails to regenerate.
The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma.
Is an important refractive component of the eye.
Has a stroma composed of randomly arranged collagen fibrils.
originalOptions: Has an endothelial layer that regenerates readily.
Has an epithelial layer that fails to regenerate.
The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma.
Is an important refractive component of the eye.
Has a stroma composed of randomly arranged collagen fibrils.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma. / D) Is an important refractive component of the eye.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: C) The endothelium actively pumps water from the stroma. / D) Is an important refractive component of the eye.
allQuestions.explanation: A) False. The human endothelium does not regenerate; dead cells are replaced by the spreading of surviving cells. B) False. The epithelial layer readily regenerates. C) True. The endothelial cells pump out ions and the water follows osmotically. Removal of water maintains corneal transparency. D) True. The cornea is a more powerful refractive element than the natural lens of the eye. E) False. The fine, equally spaced, stromal collagen fibrils are arranged in parallel and packed in an orderly manner. This is a requirement for transparency.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Retina:
options: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve.
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision.
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the retinal pigment epithelium.
The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
originalOptions: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve.
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision.
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the retinal pigment epithelium.
The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Is ten layers thick. / B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve. / E) The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A) Is ten layers thick. / B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve. / E) The RPE delivers vitamin A for rhodopsin production.
allQuestions.explanation: A) True. B) True. The retinal ganglion cell axons form the retinal nerve fibre layer and exit the eye at the optic nerve head. C) False. The rods are responsible for night vision and three cone types are responsible for daylight and colour vision. D) False. The attachment is loose; the neuroretina separates from the RPE in retinal detachment. E) True. Vitamin A is delivered by the RPE to the photoreceptors and combined with opsin.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Lens:
options: Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule.
Cortex and nucleus are rich in organelles.
Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content.
Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
originalOptions: Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule.
Cortex and nucleus are rich in organelles.
Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content.
Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Grows throughout life. / B) Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule. / D) Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content. / E) Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A) Grows throughout life. / B) Is surrounded by a collagenous capsule. / D) Has a high refractive index owing to its protein content. / E) Shape becomes more curved during accommodation for near.
allQuestions.explanation: A) True. It does grow throughout life. B) True. This is of great importance in cataract surgery. C) False. The older, deep cortical and nuclear fibres lose their nuclei and other organelles. D) True. The high protein content accounts for its high refractive index. E) True.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Suspensory ligament of the lens (the zonule):
options: Attaches the lens to the ciliary body.
Is part of the iridocorneal angle.
Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
originalOptions: Attaches the lens to the ciliary body.
Is part of the iridocorneal angle.
Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Attaches the lens to the ciliary body. / D) Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A) Attaches the lens to the ciliary body. / D) Transmits changes in tension to the lens capsule.
allQuestions.explanation: A) True. Zonular fibres extend from the pars plicata of the ciliary body to the lens equator. B) False. The zonule lies behind the iris and iridocorneal angle. C) False. The ciliary muscle contains smooth muscle, not the zonule, which is acellular. D) True. Contraction of the ciliary muscle relaxes the zonular fibres allowing the lens to increase its curvature and thus its refractive power (this is ‘accommodation’).
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Posterior chamber:
options: Is another name for the vitreous body.
Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body.
Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes.
Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
originalOptions: Is another name for the vitreous body.
Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body.
Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes.
Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body. / C) Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes. / D) Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: B) Lies between the iris, lens and ciliary body. / C) Contains aqueous humour, secreted by the ciliary processes. / D) Is in communication with the anterior chamber.
allQuestions.explanation: A) False. The vitreous body is quite separate. B) True. D) True. D) True. Communication is via the pupil, in the gap between iris and lens at the pupil margin. If this gap is narrowed or closed, pressure in the posterior chamber pushes the iris forward and may close the angle (acute closed-angle glaucoma).
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Tear film:
options: Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system.
The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea.
Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye.
originalOptions: Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system.
The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea.
Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system. / C) The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea. / D) Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye. / E) Contains lysozyme and secretory IgA.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: B) Tears are drained by the nasolacrimal system. / C) The mucoaqueous layer is in contact with the cornea. / D) Is important in the refraction of light entering the eye. / E) Contains lysozyme and secretory IgA.
allQuestions.explanation: A) False. The tear film is about 3 μm thick. B) True. There is a punctum on the medial aspect of both upper and lower eyelids. These allow tears to drain into the nasolacrimal drainage system. C) True. The mucin layer is produced by goblet cells. D) True. It provides a smooth interface for the refraction of light. E) True. These account for the antibacterial properties of the tear film.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Iridocorneal Angle:
options: Is the site of aqueous production.
Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body.
In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork.
Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
originalOptions: Is the site of aqueous production.
Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body.
In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork.
Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body. / C) In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork. / D) Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: B) Lies between the cornea and the ciliary body. / C) In primary open-angle glaucoma, there is a reduction in the number of cells covering the trabecular meshwork. / D) Fluid passes through the trabecular meshwork to Schlemm’s canal.
allQuestions.explanation: A) False. It is the site of aqueous drainage. B) True. C) True. This may reduce aqueous drainage. D) True. Flow depends on the pressure gradient between the anterior chamber and Schlemm’s canal and there is also an active component.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Optic Nerve:
options: Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate.
Is not bathed in CSF until it enters the cranial cavity.
Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries.
Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve.
Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
originalOptions: Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate.
Is not bathed in CSF until it enters the cranial cavity.
Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries.
Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve.
Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate. / C) Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries. / D) Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve. / E) Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A) Axons leave the eyeball through the cribriform plate. / C) Anteriorly is supplied by blood from the ciliary arteries. / D) Axons are not myelinated in the retrobulbar part of the nerve. / E) Is formed by axons of the nerve fibre layer of the retina.
allQuestions.explanation: A) True. This sieve-like structure provides support for the optic nerve as it leaves the eye. B) False. In the orbit, outside its pial sheath, the optic nerve is surrounded by cerebrospinal fluid within the subarachnoid space. This is in continuity with that in the intracranial cavity. C) True. The supply to the anterior part of the optic nerve differs from the supply to the anteriorlayers of the retina. D) True. This is a most important blood supply for the anterior optic nerve. E) False. They are usually not myelinated within the eye. F) True. It is made up from retinal ganglion cell axons.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: Select all the correct statements regarding the Third, Fourth and Sixth Cranial Nerves:
options: A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus.
The fourth nerve supplies the lateral rectus.
The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course.
The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
originalOptions: A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus.
The fourth nerve supplies the lateral rectus.
The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course.
The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus. / D) The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course. / E) The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: B) A nuclear third nerve palsy will cause a contralateral palsy of the superior rectus. / D) The sixth nerve has a long intracranial course. / E) The third nerve may be affected by aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery.
allQuestions.explanation: A) False. The nuclei of the sixth and seventh nerves lie in the pons. B) True. The superior rectus is innervated by the contralateral nucleus. C) False. It supplies the superior oblique. D) True. This makes the sixth nerve susceptible to trauma, which may cause lateral rectus palsy. E) True. It passes lateral to the artery.
allQuestions.lectureName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions
allQuestions.groupName: Anatomy of the Eye - Book questions

allQuestions.text: The tear film:
options: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
Is not important in the refraction of light entering the eye
originalOptions: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
Is not important in the refraction of light entering the eye
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The mucin layer is in contact with the cornea
allQuestions.explanation: The tear film is trilaminar (lipid, aqueous, mucin), with the inner mucin layer directly wetting the hydrophobic corneal epithelium — making C correct and B wrong (three layers, not four). A is wrong because the tear film average thickness is only 3 µm (ranging from 2 to 5.5 µm), not 100 µm. D is wrong because the tear-air interface is actually a major refractive surface of the eye, so the tear film is optically important, not irrelevant.

allQuestions.text: Aqueous humour is formed by:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Epithelium of ciliary body
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium of ciliary body
allQuestions.explanation: B and C are wrong because the iris and lens play no role in aqueous production — the iris only regulates pupil size, and the lens is purely refractive. D is a plausible-sounding distractor since the pars plana is part of the ciliary body region, but production occurs at the ciliary processes (pars plicata), not the pars plana. E is wrong because the trabecular meshwork is a drainage structure, not a secretory one.

allQuestions.text: All of the following statements about the tear film are true EXCEPT:
options: Lysozyme and lactoferrin in the aqueous layer provide antibacterial protection
The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
The tear film keeps the corneal surface smooth, clear, and lubricated
Conjunctival goblet cells produce the inner mucin layer
The mucin layer allows the aqueous layer to wet the hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly
originalOptions: Lysozyme and lactoferrin in the aqueous layer provide antibacterial protection
The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
The tear film keeps the corneal surface smooth, clear, and lubricated
Conjunctival goblet cells produce the inner mucin layer
The mucin layer allows the aqueous layer to wet the hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The meibomian glands produce the aqueous layer of the tear film
allQuestions.explanation: The meibomian glands, located in the tarsal plates, secrete the outer lipid layer of the tear film, not the aqueous layer — the aqueous layer (about 90% of tear thickness) comes from the main and accessory lacrimal glands, and also carries antibacterial proteins like lysozyme and lactoferrin. A, C, D, and E are all correct descriptions of tear film anatomy.

allQuestions.text: Choose the correct answer about the retina:
options: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the RPE
The RPE delivers vitamin K for rhodopsin production
originalOptions: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
Has three types of rods responsible for colour vision
The neuroretina is firmly attached to the RPE
The RPE delivers vitamin K for rhodopsin production
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Has ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerve
allQuestions.explanation: The retinal ganglion cell axons converge at the optic disc and exit the eye as the optic nerve — this is why the optic disc, lacking photoreceptors, corresponds to the physiological blind spot. A is wrong because the retina has 10 histological layers, not 7. C is wrong on two counts: colour vision is mediated by cones (not rods), and there are three types of cones (not rods). D is wrong because the neurosensory retina is only loosely apposed to the RPE (not firmly attached) — this is exactly why retinal detachment can occur. E is wrong because the RPE recycles vitamin A (not vitamin K) for the visual cycle and rhodopsin regeneration.

allQuestions.text: Most of the thickness of the cornea is formed by:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Substantia propria (stroma)
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Substantia propria (stroma)
allQuestions.explanation: The stroma (substantia propria) makes up about 90% of corneal thickness. It consists of organized collagen fibers that give the cornea its transparency and structural strength.

allQuestions.text: Cornea is supplied by nerve fibers derived from:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Trigeminal nerve
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Trigeminal nerve
allQuestions.explanation: The cornea is one of the most densely innervated tissues in the body, supplied sensorially by the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve — which is why corneal inflammation or ulceration is extremely painful.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is not a source of nutrients to the cornea?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) Vitreous humour
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Vitreous humour
allQuestions.explanation: The cornea is avascular and is nourished by atmospheric oxygen, the aqueous humour, and the perilimbal capillary network. The vitreous humour is not a source of corneal nutrition.

allQuestions.text: All of the following are avascular EXCEPT:
options: None of the above — all are avascular
originalOptions: None of the above — all are avascular
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Sclera
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Sclera
allQuestions.explanation: The cornea and lens are explicitly avascular, nourished only by diffusion, and the vitreous is a clear gel with no vessels of its own. The sclera, in contrast, is a vascularised collagenous coat — it receives blood supply (e.g. via episcleral vessels) unlike the other three purely avascular, diffusion-dependent ocular structures.

allQuestions.text: All of the following are part of the uvea except:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) Schwalbe's line
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Schwalbe's line
allQuestions.explanation: The uvea consists of the iris, ciliary body (which has two parts: pars plicata and pars plana), and the choroid. Schwalbe's line is an anatomical landmark at the anterior chamber angle (the termination of Descemet's membrane) and is not part of the uveal tract.

allQuestions.text: The following is a part of uvea except:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Bowman's membrane
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Bowman's membrane
allQuestions.explanation: Bowman's membrane is a layer of the cornea and has no relation to the uveal tract.

allQuestions.text: Optic disc diameter is:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) 1.5 mm
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: 1.5 mm
allQuestions.explanation: The optic disc diameter is used as a standard unit of measurement (Disc Diameter, DD) to describe the size and location of fundus lesions.

allQuestions.text: Aqueous humour is formed by:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Epithelium of ciliary body
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium of ciliary body
allQuestions.explanation: Aqueous humour is secreted by the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium via both active secretion and ultrafiltration.

allQuestions.text: Aqueous humor is secreted by:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Ciliary processes
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Ciliary processes
allQuestions.explanation: The ciliary processes are the precise anatomical site of aqueous humour secretion within the ciliary body.

allQuestions.text: Corneal ulceration/anaesthesia is caused by injury to the ___ cranial nerve:
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) Fifth
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Fifth
allQuestions.explanation: Loss of corneal sensation (from trigeminal nerve injury) abolishes the protective blink reflex, leaving the cornea vulnerable to neurotrophic keratitis.

allQuestions.text: Number of layers in the neurosensory retina is:
allQuestions.explanation: The neurosensory retina classically consists of 9 layers, from the photoreceptors to the nerve fiber layer. The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is anatomically and functionally a separate, tenth layer.

allQuestions.text: The cornea receives its nutrition and oxygen mainly through diffusion. Which of the following is the correct source for its oxygen supply?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Tear film
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Tear film
allQuestions.explanation: The cornea is avascular and depends entirely on diffusion for nourishment — oxygen comes from the tear film, glucose from the aqueous humour, and the limbal vessels contribute nutrients at the periphery only. This avascularity is essential for maintaining corneal transparency.

allQuestions.text: Arrange the five histological layers of the cornea in correct anterior-to-posterior order:
options: Epithelium → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Endothelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Epithelium
Epithelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Endothelium
Bowman's layer → Epithelium → Stroma → Endothelium → Descemet's membrane
originalOptions: Epithelium → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
Endothelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Epithelium
Epithelium → Descemet's membrane → Stroma → Bowman's layer → Endothelium
Bowman's layer → Epithelium → Stroma → Endothelium → Descemet's membrane
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Epithelium → Bowman's layer → Stroma → Descemet's membrane → Endothelium
allQuestions.explanation: The correct anterior-to-posterior sequence is epithelium (regenerates fast) → Bowman's layer (does not regenerate) → stroma (~90% of thickness) → Descemet's membrane (basement membrane) → endothelium (pump layer, does not regenerate).

allQuestions.text: A 32-year-old contact lens wearer with poor hygiene presents with a painful red eye. A corneal scrape grows an organism that rapidly progressed to perforation within 48 hours. Which corneal layer, if breached, is classically unable to regenerate and predisposes to permanent scarring?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Bowman's layer
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Bowman's layer
allQuestions.explanation: Bowman's layer is tough but does not regenerate if damaged, unlike the epithelium which regenerates within days. This is why deep corneal injuries involving Bowman's layer or beyond tend to leave permanent scarring rather than healing cleanly.

allQuestions.text: The main route of aqueous humour outflow, accounting for approximately 90–96% of drainage, is:
options: The uveoscleral pathway through the ciliary body face
The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
originalOptions: The uveoscleral pathway through the ciliary body face
The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal
allQuestions.explanation: Aqueous drains conventionally through the trabecular meshwork into Schlemm's canal and then into episcleral veins, accounting for the large majority of outflow; the uveoscleral route handles only about 4–10%. This conventional pathway is the main pharmacological target in glaucoma treatment.

allQuestions.text: All of the following statements about the sclera are true EXCEPT:
options: It is continuous with the cornea at the limbus
It is continuous with the dural sheath of the optic nerve posteriorly
The four rectus muscles insert into it anterior to the equator
It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
It gives the globe its shape and protects intraocular contents
originalOptions: It is continuous with the cornea at the limbus
It is continuous with the dural sheath of the optic nerve posteriorly
The four rectus muscles insert into it anterior to the equator
It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
It gives the globe its shape and protects intraocular contents
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: It is the middle vascular coat of the eye
allQuestions.explanation: The sclera is part of the outer fibrous coat (with the cornea), not the middle vascular coat — the middle vascular coat is the uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, choroid).

allQuestions.text: Which structure is responsible for producing the outer lipid layer of the tear film, and what is its main function?
options: Lacrimal gland; provides 90% of tear thickness
Goblet cells; wets the hydrophobic corneal epithelium
Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
Accessory lacrimal glands; delivers antibacterial proteins
originalOptions: Lacrimal gland; provides 90% of tear thickness
Goblet cells; wets the hydrophobic corneal epithelium
Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
Accessory lacrimal glands; delivers antibacterial proteins
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Meibomian glands; retards evaporation of the aqueous layer
allQuestions.explanation: The meibomian glands, located within the tarsal plates, secrete the outer lipid layer whose main job is to slow evaporation of the underlying aqueous layer. Dysfunction of these glands is a major cause of evaporative dry eye.

allQuestions.text: The ciliary body has two principal functions. Select the correct pair:
options: Aqueous humour drainage and pupil constriction
Refraction and pigmentation of the iris
originalOptions: Aqueous humour drainage and pupil constriction
Refraction and pigmentation of the iris
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Aqueous humour production and accommodation
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Aqueous humour production and accommodation
allQuestions.explanation: The ciliary epithelium (non-pigmented layer) produces aqueous humour, while the ciliary muscle mediates accommodation by relaxing the zonular fibres to allow the lens to become more spherical. Loss of this accommodative function with age is the basis of presbyopia.

allQuestions.text: Contraction of which iris muscle produces mydriasis (pupil dilation), and via which autonomic pathway?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Dilator pupillae; sympathetic
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Dilator pupillae; sympathetic
allQuestions.explanation: The dilator pupillae consists of radial fibres under sympathetic control, producing mydriasis, whereas the sphincter pupillae is circular and parasympathetically innervated (CN III), producing miosis.

allQuestions.text: Which statement about the lens is correct?
options: It is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
It is vascularised to support its constant growth
It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
It stops growing once the eye reaches adult size
It is fixed in position and cannot vary its power
originalOptions: It is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
It is vascularised to support its constant growth
It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
It stops growing once the eye reaches adult size
It is fixed in position and cannot vary its power
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: It contributes approximately one-third of the eye's total refractive power
allQuestions.explanation: The lens contributes about one-third of the eye's ~60 D total refractive power, with the cornea providing the other two-thirds. Unlike the cornea, the lens is the only structure able to vary its power, and it is avascular, continuing to grow throughout life by laying down new fibres.

allQuestions.text: A patient has a dense mature cataract. Which of the following visual functions is expected to be relatively preserved, helping distinguish this from glaucoma?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) Peripheral visual field
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Peripheral visual field
allQuestions.explanation: In lens or macular pathology such as cataract, central acuity is affected while the peripheral field is generally preserved — the opposite pattern to glaucoma, where the peripheral field is lost first and central acuity is preserved until late disease.

allQuestions.text: Cones, responsible for colour vision and fine visual acuity, are exclusively found at which retinal location?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) Fovea centralis
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Fovea centralis
allQuestions.explanation: Cones are concentrated at the macula and are exclusively present at its centre, the fovea centralis, which is the point of sharpest vision. Rods, by contrast, are far more numerous but absent from the very centre of the fovea, mediating dim-light and peripheral vision instead.

allQuestions.text: The optic disc corresponds to the physiological blind spot because:
options: It is the thinnest part of the retina
It is where the vitreous attaches most firmly
originalOptions: It is the thinnest part of the retina
It is where the vitreous attaches most firmly
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) It contains no photoreceptors
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: It contains no photoreceptors
allQuestions.explanation: The optic disc is where retinal ganglion cell axons converge and exit the eye as the optic nerve; since it contains no photoreceptors, it corresponds to the physiological blind spot. This is distinct from the fovea, which has the highest photoreceptor density.

allQuestions.text: The vitreous body is firmly attached at all of the following sites EXCEPT:
options: The vitreous base, just behind the ora serrata
None of the above — all are correct attachment sites
originalOptions: The vitreous base, just behind the ora serrata
None of the above — all are correct attachment sites
allQuestions.correctAnswer: D) The lens equator
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The lens equator
allQuestions.explanation: The vitreous is firmly attached at the vitreous base, the optic disc margin, and the macula — these are the sites that matter when the vitreous shrinks and pulls with age, leading to posterior vitreous detachment. It is not described as firmly attached at the lens equator.

allQuestions.text: A 68-year-old man develops sudden painless monocular vision loss. An embolus is suspected to have lodged in a branch of the ophthalmic artery. If the embolus blocks the central retinal artery rather than a posterior ciliary artery, which structure is primarily affected?
options: The optic nerve head via ischaemic optic neuropathy
originalOptions: The optic nerve head via ischaemic optic neuropathy
allQuestions.correctAnswer: C) The retina
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The retina
allQuestions.explanation: The central retinal artery supplies the retina, so its occlusion causes central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), while blockage of a posterior ciliary artery instead causes ischaemic optic neuropathy by affecting the optic nerve head and choroid. Both vessels arise from the ophthalmic artery, itself one of the first branches of the internal carotid artery.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following best describes the anterior chamber and drainage angle?
options: The space between the lens and vitreous, containing vitreous gel
The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
The space posterior to the iris, filled with vitreous
A space found only in angle-closure glaucoma
The space between the retina and choroid
originalOptions: The space between the lens and vitreous, containing vitreous gel
The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
The space posterior to the iris, filled with vitreous
A space found only in angle-closure glaucoma
The space between the retina and choroid
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The space between the cornea and iris/lens, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The space between the cornea and iris, filled with aqueous humour, with the drainage angle at the periphery
allQuestions.explanation: The anterior chamber lies between the cornea anteriorly and the iris posteriorly, filled with aqueous humour, and the drainage angle at its periphery contains the trabecular meshwork.

allQuestions.text: The conjunctiva contains goblet cells whose function is to:
options: Produce the outer lipid layer of the tear film
Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
Provide sensory innervation to the ocular surface
originalOptions: Produce the outer lipid layer of the tear film
Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
Provide sensory innervation to the ocular surface
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Secrete the mucin layer of the tear film
allQuestions.explanation: Goblet cells within the conjunctiva secrete mucin, which allows the aqueous tear layer to wet the otherwise hydrophobic corneal epithelium evenly. The conjunctiva itself has bulbar and palpebral parts meeting at the fornices.

allQuestions.text: Which of the following is the correct pairing of a uveal tract structure with its principal role?
options: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
originalOptions: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: Choroid — supplies the outer retina via the choriocapillaris
allQuestions.explanation: The choroid is the posterior, vascular part of the uveal tract, and its capillary layer (the choriocapillaris) supplies the outer retina, including the photoreceptors. New vessel growth from the choroid through Bruch's membrane is also the underlying mechanism of wet age-related macular degeneration.

allQuestions.text: A patient has an intraocular pressure of 24 mmHg on tonometry. Which of the following is the accepted normal range for IOP, against which this value should be judged?
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) 10–21 mmHg
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: 10–21 mmHg
allQuestions.explanation: The normal intraocular pressure range is 10–21 mmHg, set by the balance between aqueous production by the ciliary body and its drainage through the trabecular and uveoscleral routes. A reading of 24 mmHg is therefore above the normal range and warrants further glaucoma work-up.

allQuestions.text: Select all correct statements regarding the three concentric layers of the globe:
options: The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera
The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid
The inner neural coat is the retina
The lens forms part of the outer fibrous coat
The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
originalOptions: The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera
The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid
The inner neural coat is the retina
The lens forms part of the outer fibrous coat
The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
allQuestions.correctAnswer: A) The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera / B) The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid / C) The inner neural coat is the retina / E) The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: A) The outer fibrous coat is composed of the cornea and sclera / B) The middle vascular coat (uveal tract) includes the iris, ciliary body, and choroid / C) The inner neural coat is the retina / E) The globe wall is composed of these three concentric layers
allQuestions.explanation: A, B, C, and E are all true — the globe wall consists of an outer fibrous coat (cornea + sclera), a middle vascular coat (uveal tract: iris + ciliary body + choroid), and an inner neural coat (retina). D is false because the lens is one of the three transparent refracting media inside the globe (with aqueous humour and vitreous), not part of the wall itself.

allQuestions.text: Regarding the refractive power of the eye, which statement is correct?
options: The lens contributes roughly two-thirds and the cornea one-third of total refractive power
The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
The vitreous is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
The sclera contributes significantly to refraction
Refractive power is equally divided among the cornea, lens, and vitreous
originalOptions: The lens contributes roughly two-thirds and the cornea one-third of total refractive power
The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
The vitreous is the eye's most powerful refractive structure
The sclera contributes significantly to refraction
Refractive power is equally divided among the cornea, lens, and vitreous
allQuestions.correctAnswer: B) The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
allQuestions.correctAnswerText: The cornea contributes roughly two-thirds and the lens one-third of total refractive power
allQuestions.explanation: The cornea provides about two-thirds of the eye's total refractive power (~43 D of the ~60 D total), while the lens contributes the remaining third — though only the lens can vary its own power for accommodation. This distribution is a frequently tested high-yield fact in ophthalmic optics.
